chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from the one who reported it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the man who prays while gesturing upon his animal, he (peace be upon him) said: 'He should uncover the place of prostration.'

key_terms.مَوْضِعَ السُّجُودِ: the place of prostration (specifically the forehead area)
key_terms.يُومِئُ: gesturing (indicating bowing and prostration with head movements)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for uncovering the prostration spot when praying on an animal?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the practical application of prayer while traveling (salat al-musafir), emphasizing that the physical requirement of forehead contact with the earth (turbah) is maintained even when seated on a mount. It highlights the Shia juristic principle that the 'spot of prostration' must be exposed and pure, ensuring the validity of the gesture (i'rad) despite the mobility of the rider. This ruling underscores the balance between ease in travel and the preservation of essential prayer conditions.
